key_insight: Rotationally symmetric gradient operators improve pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann accuracy and reduce spurious currents near walls misaligned with the lattice.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports more accurate multiphase simulations of capillary transport and porous-media imbibition without extending the lattice stencil for higher-order gradients.
method: Compute coupling-force density gradients using rotationally symmetric convolution operators.
Compare fluid–solid coupling applied through both fluids versus through one fluid.
Benchmark against the classical lattice-weights approach.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved accuracy across wall-droplet benchmarks, capillary-rise tests evaluated against Jurin’s law, and porous-media imbibition.
watch_item: The preferred fluid–solid interaction variant is problem-dependent; the abstract provides no quantitative error reductions or computational costs.
paper_title: Rotationally Symmetric Lattice Boltzmann Pseudopotential Methods for Porous Media Applications
